incidents.title: Checkout authorization timeouts
incidents.summary: Checkout success fell while payment latency remained within its normal band.

incidents.title: Retry storm amplified payment errors
incidents.summary: Immediate checkout retries multiplied payment-provider load.

incidents.title: Stale inventory reservations
incidents.summary: An extended cache lifetime served stale availability during a stock event.

incidents.title: Fraud enrichment latency blocked payments
incidents.summary: Synchronous enrichment exhausted fraud-service workers and delayed authorizations.

sections.heading: Establish the failing boundary
sections.text: Compare checkout timeout rate with payment authorization latency. If checkout timeouts rise while payment p95 stays below 800 milliseconds, inspect the checkout client timeout and the most recent checkout deployment before escalating to the payment provider.

sections.heading: Safe checks
sections.text: Diff the active checkout configuration against the preceding version. Inspect timeout and retry values. A rollback is a proposed mitigation only after the deployment correlation is confirmed by an operator.

sections.heading: Disconfirming signal
sections.text: If payment authorization p95 rises above 2500 milliseconds across providers, treat the provider or payment path as the primary hypothesis rather than a checkout-client timeout.

sections.heading: Trace dependants
sections.text: Start from the degraded service and traverse incoming DEPENDS_ON relationships to at most three hops. Prioritize tier-one dependants and report asynchronous consumers separately from synchronous request paths.

sections.heading: Validate impact
sections.text: A topology path represents plausible exposure, not observed failure. Confirm each service with an alert, error-rate change, or user-journey signal before declaring it impacted.

sections.heading: Cache validation
sections.text: Compare cache TTL and reservation conflict rate around the first alert. Purge or rollback only after confirming stale version tokens in sampled reservation responses.

sections.heading: Downstream checks
sections.text: Inspect cart availability mismatch and checkout inventory-rejection rate. Preserve the distinction between cached availability and the authoritative reservation result.

sections.heading: Worker saturation
sections.text: Inspect fraud worker utilization, enrichment dependency latency, and queue age. Synchronous enrichment can propagate latency to payment authorization even when the provider is healthy.

sections.heading: Containment proposal
sections.text: Propose disabling optional synchronous enrichment or restoring the prior worker policy. Execution requires human approval and a change record.

postmortems.title: INC-087 — Retry storm after checkout release

sections.heading: Root cause
sections.text: Deployment dep-0870 enabled three immediate payment retries in Checkout API. A transient provider error therefore became four near-simultaneous requests, saturating the payment path and reducing checkout success.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.text: Checkout retry rate and provider request volume rose six minutes after deployment. Payment latency increased with request volume. Rolling back dep-0870 returned both signals to baseline.

sections.heading: Learning
sections.text: Retries require exponential backoff, jitter, and a shared budget. A recent deployment plus correlated downstream saturation is stronger evidence than deployment timing alone.

postmortems.title: INC-063 — Inventory cache served stale availability

sections.heading: Root cause
sections.text: Deployment dep-0630 increased Inventory API cache TTL from one minute to fifteen minutes. During a stock event, carts displayed stale availability and authoritative reservations failed.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.text: Reservation conflicts rose nineteen minutes after deployment, followed by cart availability mismatches. Payment latency and fraud-service health remained normal.

sections.heading: Learning
sections.text: Availability caches must preserve stock-version tokens and use event-driven invalidation. A cart symptom can originate in the inventory dependency rather than Cart Service itself.

postmortems.title: INC-041 — Synchronous fraud enrichment exhausted workers

sections.heading: Root cause
sections.text: Deployment dep-0410 moved optional fraud feature enrichment into the synchronous scoring path. Slow enrichment calls saturated fraud workers and propagated latency through Payment API to Checkout API.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.text: Fraud worker utilization reached 99 percent before payment authorization p95 crossed four seconds. Disabling synchronous enrichment restored worker capacity and payment latency.

sections.heading: Learning
sections.text: Graph topology identified the propagation path fraud-service to payment-api to checkout-api to edge-gateway. Each hop was confirmed with its own telemetry before inclusion in the observed blast radius.
